items.target: tools/ui-invariants.mjs, checks S1/S15 (the 3-line allowance) and S18 (the 60% floor)
items.problem: Two of this round's bounds are constants fitted to today's content on surfaces the build regenerates, in a loop whose charter forbids changing content - so when either fires there is no permitted remedy and the red will be misread as a presentation regression. Measured by me on the shipped build. (a) S1/S15's 3-line allowance: all four /blog titles wrap to exactly 3 lines at a track measuring exactly 384.0px. Three of three. A post whose title is one line longer than the current longest (117 characters) turns S15 red, and neither available lever is permitted - widening --measure-list was rejected with cause in R7's own addendum, and shortening the title is a content edit. (b) S18's 60% floor: .home-side 1079.3px, .rail-changes 1230.8px, ratio 87.7%. The feed is 24 entries: 23 at 43.4px and one annotated at 209.3px. S18 fires when the feed exceeds 1079.3 / 0.6 = 1798.8px, which is 568px of headroom - 3.4 more annotated entries in the top 24. data/changes.jsonl is regenerated daily; a day with five annotated changes takes the home page's gate red with no presentation remedy left, since the rail's content is now fully committed and relocating a second section is not a repeatable move. Neither bound is wrong, and both are structurally sound, which I verified adversarially: forcing /data's track to 350px (only 34px under the cap, wrapping just 2 lines) fires the COLLAPSED branch, and forcing /blog's to 350px at exactly 3 lines fires it too, so the line allowance genuinely cannot mask an undersized track. The defect is not the bound; it is that a bound with zero declared headroom reports PASS without saying how close it is - D2's own lesson (read what a check MEASURED, not its verdict line) applied to a margin instead of to a coverage ratio.
items.evidence: measured by me with Playwright against out/ (four /blog .rail-title elements at 3 client rects each on a 384.0px track; /data's one 2-line label on a 384.0px track; .home-side 1079.3px vs .rail-changes 1230.8px with 24 feed entries at 209.3 / 43.4px); falsification runs I executed: --only S1 --break '.browse{grid-template-columns:350px auto auto}' and --only S15 --break '.rail-posts .rail-item{grid-template-columns:100px 350px}', both firing on the collapsed branch
items.invariant: Every check whose threshold is derived from the artifact's current content prints its remaining headroom alongside its PASS - the measured worst case, the bound, and the margin between them - and records in its falsifier the content assumption the bound rests on, so a future failure is diagnosable as content growth rather than as a presentation regression.
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R7 (iter-07 addendum, which states the 3-line bound as 'the largest line count either bounded surface's real content presently needs' - the word 'presently' is the whole of this finding) and RULES.md R13 (iter-07 addendum a)
items.prescription: Have S1, S15 and S18 print their margin on success, not only their message on failure: for S15, 'worst case 3 of 3 lines allowed - NO HEADROOM'; for S18, 'shorter side at 87.7% of taller, floor 60%, headroom 568px of feed growth'. That alone converts a silent cliff into a visible one and costs nothing. Then record in each falsifier what the bound assumes about content and what the loop should do when it is exceeded - for S15, that a 4-line title signals the surface has outgrown --measure-list on that template and needs its own token rather than a widened shared one; for S18, that a feed grown past 1798.8px signals .home-grid's split needs a different mechanism, not more rail content. Do NOT loosen either bound to buy headroom: a bound relaxed in advance of the case that would test it is exactly the miscalibration iter-06 retired the occupancy clause for.

items.problem: Unchanged. The viewport-coupled fidelity detector is keyed to one CSS signature - an element whose computed position is sticky and whose max-height is vh-based - so it catches the one case already known (#catalog-table-wrap, correctly labelled this run) and would not catch a second instance built differently. D9's own generalisation is that identity is not fidelity; the current detector proves fidelity for exactly one known shape and asserts nothing about any other.
items.evidence: loops/ui-loop/evidence/current/manifest.json (only the two /catalog 1440 entries carry capture:'viewport'); JUDGE.md L5
items.invariant: The evidence rig detects a misrendering fullPage capture by comparing the rendered image against the page's live DOM geometry, not by matching a CSS signature: for each capture, at least one measured element's live bounding box agrees with its position in the captured image within a stated tolerance.
items.prescription: Replace the signature match with a differential check: capture at viewport size and at fullPage, measure one high-signal element's box live in each, and label the capture 'viewport' whenever the two disagree beyond tolerance. That detects the class rather than the instance, and it folds naturally into I13's geometry record since both need the same evaluate() call.

items.problem: Unchanged and still unresolvable by this loop. /catalog presents 396 rows as one continuous surface with four filter controls and no pagination or grouping. Whether a reader can find one model among 396 by filtering rather than by paging is a question about a real person's behaviour, which no screenshot, no axe run and no focus traversal answers. Listed so it stops resurfacing as actionable.
items.prescription: Keeper measurement: put the filter-only surface in front of real readers with a find-this-model task and measure time-to-target against a paged or grouped alternative. Not implementable from presentation evidence.

items.problem: The second clause of I8's invariant - 'a value constant across the collection is stated once for the collection, not once per row' - cannot be satisfied by this loop and should stop being carried as though it could. The Read column still renders 396 identical date strings occupying 105.2px of the table's 1152px, and removing them is blocked not by presentation but by specs/directory's per-row provenance requirement, documented in lib/catalog.mjs's catalogRow doc comment and untouched by the I8 change, which correctly altered only the render layer's treatment. Slot 1 forbids changing what a page says. Recorded as a keeper so it is not re-filed as actionable, and so a future round that does own the spec can pick it up with the reasoning intact.
items.evidence: lib/render/catalog.mjs (the Read cell renders row.fetched unconditionally); lib/catalog.mjs catalogRow doc comment; measured by me: 396 of 396 rows carry the string '2026-08-31', column width 105.2px
items.governing_rule: RULES.md R8 (the badge clause's own analogue; its value half is out of this loop's reach, its weight half is I36)
items.prescription: Content/spec gate. If per-row provenance is genuinely required for machine consumers, satisfy it in the data layer (the row already carries source_url in /catalog.json) and let the rendered table state the collection default once, as renderFetchLine already does above the table. That is a specs/directory decision, not a presentation one.
